sections.h2: What does the Chester County Recorder of Deeds do when a house sells?
sections.html:
The office in West Chester files the deed that moves a Chester County house from seller to buyer, collects the realty transfer tax due on that deed, and keeps the permanent land record. Until a deed is recorded here, the public record still shows the old owner, which can stall a buyer's loan or a later resale.

The county describes the office as the custodian of all land records and indexes for transfers, going back to 1688. It also records mortgages, satisfactions, powers of attorney, subdivision plans and notary commissions. The tax money it collects is passed on to the Commonwealth, the county's 73 municipalities and its 14 school districts. Staff cannot draft a deed, search for liens or give legal advice, so the drafting usually falls to a title company or attorney.

sections.h2: Where is the Recorder of Deeds office and when can I file?
sections.html:
The office is at 313 W. Market Street, Suite 3302, West Chester, and the phone number listed on the county page is 610-344-6330. It is open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., but documents for recording must be handed in by 4 p.m.

  • Same-day recording runs 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • Same-day recording of large exhibits such as maps and subdivision plans stops at 3:00 p.m.
  • The search library is open until 4:15 p.m.
  • Fees must be paid at the moment of recording, and the office will not record an unofficial copy of a document that is already on record.

Bring a self-addressed stamped envelope with any paper filing. The county adds postage and a $2.00 fee when one is missing.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Chester County?
sections.html:
A standard deed costs $94.75 to record under the schedule effective December 1, 2025. That base covers one UPI, up to four pages, one notation fee and four names. The same base applies to a mortgage and to a deed of correction.

Chester County recording fees, schedule effective December 1, 2025 (source: Chester County Recorder of Deeds)
DocumentBase fee
Deed$94.75
Re-recorded deed or mortgage$96.75
Deed in blank or relocation deed$183.50
Satisfaction, assignment, release, easement$81.75
Power of attorney$20.50
Miscellaneous document$40.50

Extras stack on top. A UPI costs $20.00 per number, a document that misses the PRIA formatting standards carries a $25.00 non-compliance fee, and each exhibit adds $5.00. The base fee already contains a $41.25 judicial administration charge set by the Department of Revenue.

sections.h2: What is the transfer tax on a Chester County sale and who pays it?
sections.html:
The county fee page puts the rate at 1% of the consideration or computed value, whichever is higher, with higher rates in three places: Malvern and Tredyffrin at 1.5%, and Coatesville at 2.5%. Ask the recorder for the combined state and local figure that applies to your deed.

State law makes both the grantor and the grantee jointly liable for the tax, and the Department of Revenue notes that certain family transfers and property passed by will or intestacy are exempt. Who covers the bill in a sale is a matter for the sales agreement.

  • Transfer tax is paid by separate checks, one for the municipality and one for the state, made out to the Chester County Recorder of Deeds.
  • Only business checks, cashier's checks and money orders are taken for tax. Cash and credit cards are refused for tax.
  • Recording fees go on a third check or other accepted payment.

sections.h2: What payment and paperwork rules cause rejected deeds?
sections.html:
Most rejections come from payment mistakes and missing page-one details. The recorder takes cash in person for recording fees only, and personal, estate and trustee checks are refused at all times. Checks older than 180 days are not accepted, no more than ten documents may share one check, and a returned check triggers a $25 bank fee on top of the $10.00 rejection fee for returned documents.

  • Type a valid UPI on the first page. A computer-printed label on page one is acceptable.
  • State the grantee's exact mailing address and certify it with a signature, as 16 P.S. Section 9781 requires.
  • Attach a Statement of Value when the deed does not state the full value, unless a family exemption applies. The Common Level Ratio factor, updated each July 1, belongs on that form.
  • For land in more than one municipality, show the local tax split in dollars on the deed.
  • Match every name across the caption, signature and notary acknowledgment, including Sr., Jr. and III.

sections.h2: What should a Chester County seller check before the deed goes in?
sections.html:
Start with the title trail. A prior mortgage that was paid off should show a recorded satisfaction, and the satisfaction, assignment and release category carries its own $81.75 base fee if one is missing. If the house came through an estate, the Statement of Value and the family-transfer rules matter more than they do on an ordinary sale, so the title company should review them early.

Also confirm the grantee's mailing address with the buyer. Tax bills are sent to the address on the deed, and the county asks that it be exact, current, legible and scannable. A deed sent in with a tax check from a personal or estate account will be turned away, so closing funds for transfer tax should be arranged as a cashier's check or money order ahead of time.

  • Order a copy of the vesting deed from the recording office if the seller's own copy is lost. Certified copies run $0.50 per page plus $5.00 for certification when made by staff.
  • Ask the title company whether the property sits in Malvern, Tredyffrin or Coatesville, where the higher tax rates apply.
  • Confirm the deed shows the correct UPI and not the tax parcel number, since the two are formatted differently.

sections.h2: Can a Chester County deed be e-recorded?
sections.html:
Yes. Chester County takes electronic filings through Simplifile and CSC eRecording, which is how most title companies deliver a closing package. For a deed that owes tax, the consideration and the state and municipal tax amounts must appear on the first page.

Each package is limited to ten documents, and a single document cannot list more than ten UPI numbers. E-recording is not available for deeds of correction, re-recorded deeds or Statements of Value with exhibits attached. Those go in on paper. Resubmitting a document costs a $10 return fee each time, and a document recorded in error is not refunded.

sections.h2: What does the Chester County housing market look like for sellers?
sections.html:
Chester County sits in the Philadelphia metropolitan area, with West Chester as the seat and Coatesville as its only city. The Census Bureau estimated 557,116 residents in July 2025 across about 751 square miles of Piedmont hills and valleys, with 217,440 housing units.

For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau reports a median owner-occupied home value of $485,600, a median household income of $127,208 and median gross rent of $1,763. Owners occupy 75.1% of homes. Houses in the south of the county, in the Brandywine and Octoraro watersheds, sell alongside suburban homes near the Main Line, so transfer tax can differ sharply from one township to the next.

faqs.q: How long does it take to record a deed in Chester County?
faqs.a: Same-day recording is offered until 4:00 p.m. on business days, and e-recorded packages through Simplifile or CSC are the usual route for closings. Large plans must arrive by 3:00 p.m. for same-day handling.

faqs.q: Can I pay the Chester County transfer tax by credit card?
faqs.a: No. Transfer tax must be paid by business check, cashier's check or money order made out to the Chester County Recorder of Deeds. Credit cards may be used only for recording fees and copy requests, with a 3.5% in-person fee.

faqs.q: Do I need a Statement of Value to record a deed in Chester County?
faqs.a: Yes, when the deed does not state the full and complete value of the property, unless a family exemption applies. It is a Department of Revenue form and is recorded with the deed, so its pages count toward the recording fee.

faqs.q: Can the Recorder of Deeds correct a mistake in a recorded deed?
faqs.a: Not by editing it. A deed of correction costs $94.75 and needs a written explanation on page one, the book and page of the deed being fixed, a new acknowledgment and a Statement of Value. Deeds of correction cannot be e-recorded.

faqs.q: Is the transfer tax the same everywhere in Chester County?
faqs.a: No. The listed rate is 1% of consideration or computed value, but Malvern and Tredyffrin charge 1.5% and Coatesville charges 2.5%. Check the municipality where the house sits before you price a sale.
